headline: High: open-webui’s broad networked tool surface can ingest and act on content while awesome-python is a non-runnable docs-only collection, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risk if paired through shared files or MCP.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui exposes MCP, plugins, and tool servers plus file inputs, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content; awesome-python is a docs-only repository with no runnable safeguards or isolation. The pair has no documented direct bridge, so the pathway is inferred rather than observed, but shared files or copied content could be treated as instructions.
conditions: IF awesome-python content is copied into open-webui prompts or files
IF open-webui MCP or plugin tools parse imported text as instructions
IF a shared workspace is used to move content between the two
mitigations: Disable MCP/plugins for the session
Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Use a read-only export of any shared files
Strip instructions from imported text before loading
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches documents, notes, files, persistent memory, and API keys, and can access local files or mounted volumes; awesome-python is a repository/docs artifact that could be placed in the same workspace. That creates a plausible shared-workspace leakage path, though the pairwise bridge is not directly documented and the first agent itself has no egress.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same local directory or mounted volume
IF sensitive files are present in that shared workspace
IF open-webui is configured to ingest local files or documents
mitigations: Separate the storage locations immediately
Remove secrets from any shared directory
Run open-webui without file ingestion for the session
Audit mounted volumes for sensitive content
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui has broad network egress, browser, subprocess, and file capabilities, while awesome-python is non-runnable and does not itself write. There is no direct write-write conflict, but open-webui can still contend over shared files or external resources if the collection is used as a workspace index or artifact store; uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF open-webui is allowed to modify files or artifacts in that directory
IF external resources are shared through the same API credentials
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Make the collection repository read-only
Rotate shared API keys before co-running
Pause subprocess-heavy workflows during overlap
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can render or act on model outputs through tools, MCP, and function calling, so if it consumes content derived from awesome-python as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream actions. awesome-python itself is only a collection, but the pair still forms an unsafe producer-consumer chain when open-webui treats imported content as trusted without verification.
conditions: IF open-webui uses content sourced from awesome-python as facts or instructions
IF open-webui forwards that content into tools, browsers, or APIs without verification
IF downstream actions are enabled in the same session
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution
Mark imported repository content as untrusted
Disable auto-action workflows for the session
Cross-check claims against primary sources
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool calls

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, documents, notes, files, and persistent memory, while awesome-python is a public open-source repository. If regulated or sensitive material is placed into open-webui, its broader storage and third-party API surface can create retention or residency mismatches; the other agent is not cited because it is only a public docs collection.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui
IF open-webui sends that data to external APIs or stores it in persistent memory
IF the repository content is mixed with sensitive operational data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of open-webui
Disable persistent memory for sensitive sessions
Review API destinations before use
Purge stored chats after the task
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
